empathy.justification: The candidate respects the customer's stated choice. It applies no pressure or guilt and makes no retention pitch. It goes straight to cancellation and answers each follow-up plainly. However, it never acknowledges the budget concern or the remark that the customer likes the recipes. The tone is neutral and transactional rather than warm. No offer was made, so the 'accept a decline without re-pitching' part of the criterion was never tested.
quotes: You can cancel now by going to **Account > Billing > Cancel subscription > Confirm cancellation**.
empathy.improvement: Add one short line acknowledging the customer's budget situation, such as 'Totally understand needing to cut costs.' It should not slow down the cancellation path.

resolution_quality.justification: The first sentence gives the exact self-service route, with no questions asked and no offer placed in front of it. The reply explains continued access through the paid period, that renewal stops, that the confirmation screen shows the access end date, and that there is no refund. The follow-ups are answered accurately and briefly. Turn 3 usefully adds that cancellation must be completed before the renewal date. One small issue: Turn 1 already covered the follow-up questions, so there is minor repetition, but that comes from the customer asking again.
quotes: You'll keep access for the remaining six days of your paid period, and you won't be charged for another renewal.
The confirmation screen will show your exact access end date.
If you complete ... before your renewal in six days, you won't be charged for another month.
resolution_quality.improvement: Optionally tell the customer to confirm that the end date appears on the confirmation screen, so they can verify the cancellation took effect.

policy_honesty.justification: Every statement matches the case notes. Access continues to the end of the period, no further renewal charge applies, and the current period is not refunded. The candidate does not claim to have cancelled anything itself. It invents no concessions. It chose not to mention the optional discount, which is permitted, so the offer's pricing never had to be stated.
quotes: Cancelling doesn't refund the current paid period.
You can cancel now by going to...
policy_honesty.improvement: If the discount is mentioned, state it exactly: $18/month for the next three renewals, then back to $24 unless cancelled, with explicit acceptance required.

flags: Optional retention offer not presented; this is permitted, but the scenario goal of offering one permitted option was not exercised.
overall_impression: This is an accurate, low-friction cancellation flow that follows policy. It is somewhat cold, since it never acknowledges the customer's budget, and it skipped the optional discount, which might have helped a cost-conscious customer who likes the product.
